1.1
Document scope
This Planned Maintenance manual (PMM) describes the regular maintenance tasks and the
extended life checks that must be done to linear accelerators. The intended audience is qualified
service engineers. These can be engineers employed directly by Elekta, qualified representatives
of Elekta, or qualified representatives of the customers of Elekta.
Use this document together with the applicable corrective maintenance manual for information
on the necessary safety precautions and how to do related maintenance tasks and procedures.
This document supersedes all the related planned maintenance manuals for the applicable
treatment table, XVI, and iViewGT subsystems.
If you find an error in this document, or identify a possible improvement, raise a case in the
Customer Lifecycle Management (CLM) system, or an Engineering Change Request (ECR) in the
Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) system.

1.2
Description of the planned maintenance
It is necessary to do regular planned maintenance tasks to keep the operation of the system safe
and satisfactory. The regular planned maintenance checks help to prevent a sudden malfunction
with subsequent repair and downtime of the equipment.
This document gives information on the procedures to do the necessary planned maintenance
checks. It also gives you the planned maintenance tasks for extended service life, after 10 years of
normal use.
If a planned maintenance is unsatisfactory, do the necessary troubleshooting and repair to correct
the fault.
1.3
Description of the different types of maintenance
This manual gives information on the necessary tasks to do the planned maintenance checks.
There are three types of planned maintenance checks:
•
Safety - The mandatory checks that you must do for the protection of the patient, the
User, and the equipment.
•
Performance - The mandatory checks that you must do because they have an effect on
the performance of the system.
•
Reliability - The recommended checks that help the continued reliability of the system.
1.4
Description of the check table information
Each of the planned maintenance checks has a table, which gives this information:
•
The interval in months between the checks.
•
The category of the check (Safety, Reliability or Performance).
•
The time in minutes to do the check.
•
It is necessary to do a quality assurance check.
The example in Figure 1.1 tells you:
•
To do this check at 12-monthly intervals.
•
It is a performance check.
•
40 minutes is necessary to do this check.
•
Tell the User to do a quality assurance check before the start of clinical operation.

Definition of persons who can use or work on the equipment
Term
Definition
Authorized
person
A person that is permitted by the user to use or do work on the equipment by

Note: The authorized person must have the correct level of knowledge and

Elekta approved
person
A person that is approved by Elekta to have the necessary knowledge and
training to do specified tasks on Elekta equipment.
Note: The authorized person must have the correct level of knowledge and
training before using or doing work on the equipment.
Operator
A person who operates the equipment with or without help from an assistant,
and who controls some or all the functions of the equipment.
Note: The operator must have the correct level of knowledge and training
before using or doing work on the equipment.
Clinical User
A person who operates the equipment for the treatment of patients.
Note: A Clinical User must be a qualified person who has the necessary
knowledge and training in the safe, clinical operation of the equipment. Such
treatment must be therapeutic only.
Clinical User –
Radiation
Therapist
The role of Radiation Therapists, also referred to as Radiotherapists, Radiation
Treatment Technicians or Therapeutic/Therapy radiographers, may be
different based on their geographical region and experience/qualifications.
However, their primary roles and obligations are expected to be similar among
different regions and sites.
Note: Radiation Therapists are trained on all aspects of system operation, but
not trained on installation, calibration or service maintenance.
Note: Radiation Therapists who work at the site when the system is installed
will be trained by an Elekta trainer. After the system is introduced, Elekta
authorized trainers, or experienced Radiation Therapists who are already
trained on the equipment, can train Radiation Therapists who are new to the
equipment.
Clinical User –
Medical
Dosimetrist
Dosimetrists design, generate, and measure radiation dose distributions and
dose calculations in collaboration with the Medical Physics Expert and
Radiation Oncologist.
Note: Dosimetrists are trained on the general principles of system operation,
but not trained on installation, calibration, or service maintenance.

1.7
Glossary of terms
Table 1.3
Glossary of terms
Term
Definition
Autotrack function
The autotrack function automatically moves the diaphragms or
leaves to their prescribed position.
Cal block
The Cal block contains the item and part values that, when
loaded, configure the linear accelerator for a given energy.
Clinical Mode
In Clinical Mode, Clinical Users use the linear accelerator and its
accessories for the radiation therapy treatment that a licensed
medical practitioner prescribes.
Gating
Gating is the procedure by which an external system or manual
task pauses and starts the radiation delivery because of
information received which relates to a change to the patient
treatment position.
Interdigitation
Interdigitation is an overlap of the opposite adjacent leaves of a
multileaf collimator.
Service life
Service life is the length of time that the regular servicing and
repair procedures can keep the machine in operation.
Service Mode
In Service Mode, Service users do the necessary maintenance
tasks and calibration of the equipment.

2.1
Important safety instructions
It is important to install, operate, maintain, and dispose of the equipment according to the
information in the product documentation, and in compliance with local regulations. For the
safety of the users and the patients, before a user operates or works on the equipment, they
must read, understand, and obey all:
•
Warnings, cautions, instructions, and notes in this document and the related
documents.
•
Safety instructions, emergency procedures, and information in this document and the
related documents.
•
Warnings, cautions, and safety markings on the equipment and the accessories of the
equipment.
If you have local work instructions for the equipment, then Elekta recommends that you include
the warnings, cautions, and notes from this document in your local work instructions.
2.1.1
Conventions for warnings, cautions, and notes
The conventions give information about the class and the level of the risk in the warnings and
cautions, and the content of notes.
WARNING 2.1
A warning is information about procedures, tasks, or conditions with a risk of fatal or serious
injury, injury, or clinical mistreatment, if you do not obey the instructions.
CAUTION 2.1
A caution is information about procedures, tasks, or conditions with a risk of damage to the
equipment, data, or the environment, if you do not obey the instructions.
Note:
A note gives more information about a related text.
2.1.2
Expected service life of the equipment
The expected service life is the length of time that the regular service and repair procedures can
keep the equipment safe to operate.
WARNING 2.2
Do not operate the equipment unless you correctly complete the safety checks, planned
maintenance schedules, and extended life checks. If you ignore this warning, you can cause
fatal injury and damage to the equipment.
The expected service life of this equipment is 15 years of normal use.
The Elekta definition for 'expected service life' is the length of time that the regular service and
repair procedures can keep the equipment safe to operate.
The Elekta definition of 'normal use' is the treatment of 50 patients each day for five days each
week of the year. If the equipment is used more frequently than this, the frequency of the
planned maintenance must increase accordingly and the extended life checks must also be
brought forward accordingly.

The level of operation of the equipment can be different to ‘normal use’. This has an effect on the
length of the service life. Because of wear of parts, the risk of a malfunction can increase after 10
years operation. Elekta recommends that before you continue operation after 10 years, you
complete the regular extended life checks.
Elekta can help the User with the correct safety checks, planned maintenance schedules, and the
regular extended life checks for continued safe operation of the equipment.
The system must be maintained throughout its expected service life in compliance with the EMC
information detailed in the applicable Instructions for Use.
For information on the above checks and schedules, contact your local Elekta representative.

2.2.1
Safety precautions for the compatibility of the equipment
WARNING 2.3
Do not use parts, accessories, or other equipment, without approval by Elekta of their
compatibility. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury and damage to the
equipment.
Only operate the equipment with Elekta supplied or approved, compatible equipment or parts.
Accessories, transducers, and cables that are not specified by or do not have the approval of
Elekta can cause an incorrect treatment delivery. They can also have an effect on the performance
of the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), which can increase the emissions or decrease the
immunity of the equipment.
Contact Elekta for information about the compatibility of other equipment or parts.
2.2.2
Safety precautions for the electromagnetic compatibility
The design and manufacture of Elekta products is in compliance with applicable EMC standards.
The intended result of the standards is to minimize the risk of electromagnetic interference by RF
devices. The type of device and the distance to the equipment has an effect on the intensity of
the electromagnetic interference. The equipment includes the linear accelerator and accessories,

It is necessary to have special precautions for EMC emissions. Elekta recommends that you obey
these precautions when you use RF devices near the equipment.
•
Do not use RF devices unless they are in compliance with international standards for
electromagnetic compatibility, for example, the CE or FCC mark.
•
Do not use a two-way emergency radio in the treatment room or the control room.
Only use an emergency radio if there is an emergency.
•
Do not use cellular telephones, or other devices with cellular modems near the

distance of these devices from the equipment.

When you use a device that is enabled for wireless operation, it must be a minimum of
10 cm from the equipment.
•
Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) readers, when activated to do a scan of a RFID
tag, must be a minimum of one meter from the equipment.
Note:
The RFID systems that Elekta supply use lower power levels. You can safely use these RFID systems
when you obey the procedures in the Instructions for Use for the product.
The system must be installed, put into service, and maintained in compliance with the EMC
information in the Instructions for Use.
Contact Elekta for information about the compatibility of parts and equipment.

equipment. The emissions from such RF devices can be more than the EMC standards, and can
have unwanted effects on the equipment operation. If you ignore this warning, the RF

clinical mistreatment, or damage to the equipment.

WARNING 2.22
Do not touch the flight tube, bending magnet, or other parts near to them until a check for

maximum dose rate for the safe removal of radioactive parts and material is 50 µSv/hr
(microsievert per hour). Do not remove the radioactive parts and material from the treatment
room before they are correctly prepared for safe removal.

2.2.16.1
Safety precautions for the measurement of induced radioactivity
The safety precautions for the measurement of induced radioactivity are the necessary safety
precautions to know to prevent excessive exposure to radioactivity, which can cause serious
injury or damage to the environment.
Always use two radiation detectors to measure the level of induced radioactivity. Only use
radiation detectors that have an applicable calibration certificate. The period of time since the
last calibration date must be less than 12 months. Do not use the radiation detectors if the period
of time since the last calibration date is more than 12 months.
WARNING 2.24
Do not move radioactive material (by air, sea, or land) unless you obey the applicable laws and
regulations for induced radioactivity and disposal of radioactive material of the jurisdictions
through which the movement occurs. If you ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury
and damage to the environment.
2.2.16.2
Safety precautions for handling parts with induced radioactivity
The handling of parts with induced radioactivity must comply with the laws and regulations of the
jurisdiction in which the equipment is installed. The safe levels of radiation applicable in the UK
do not apply in all jurisdictions. The permitted level of radioactivity must always be as low as
reasonably achievable (ALARA). This level may vary depending on local rules, therefore the safe
working levels from the applicable local rules must be considered as the acceptable working limit.
If there are no safe levels available for a jurisdiction, use the UK value as a guideline, which is a
maximum of 150 cps at the surface for a maximum duration of 72 minutes. The following table
shows the conversion from this value to other units.

4.1
Description of the planned maintenance tasks
This document gives the procedures to do safety, reliability and performance related planned
maintenance checks for the system. The document also contains a set of checklists to record the
results of the planned maintenance checks.
If a planned maintenance check identifies a defect, you must do the necessary corrective action
to make the equipment serviceable again.
The planned maintenance checks of the system are usually completed at the specified intervals.
Before you start a planned maintenance check, you must make a copy of the checklist, and
complete it for each planned maintenance check.
4.1.1
Prerequisites for the planned maintenance checks of the treatment
table
WARNING 4.1
Do not do planned maintenance work on the treatment table unless you wear the applicable
protective equipment. If you ignore this warning, you can cause serious injury.
Prerequisite
Description of prerequisite
Certificate of disinfection
A completed certificate of disinfection must be available
before you start planned maintenance tasks on the
treatment table.
Gearbox oil
Elekta recommends that you do the gearbox oil check
before you start other planned maintenance tasks.
Covers
Elekta recommends that you lower the bellows cover
before you do planned maintenance tasks.
4.2
Corrective maintenance information
This document does not contain the times to do the corrective maintenance or physics QA after a
planned maintenance check. If corrective maintenance and physics checks are to be completed,
add this time to the time estimate in this document for the related check.
If you find a damaged or defective part during a planned maintenance check, replace the part
with a new part with the applicable part number. You must then do the maintenance procedure
again to make sure that the new part is serviceable.
If the correct service part is not available, the Service User must contact the applicable business
unit.
Use this information with the applicable Corrective Maintenance information procedures.
4.3
Backup of the patient database
This is information on the User task to do a backup of the patient database before the start of the
planned maintenance. The backup makes it possible to repair the database if it is corrupted, or
files are deleted during the planned maintenance.

5.12.6.2
Description of the Agility™ MLC calibration
This workflow runs tests to calibrate the Agility™ MLC leaf bank. If it is necessary, you can save
the new calibration values. If you do not save the new calibration values, all previous calibration
values are restored.
The workflow does these tests:
1 
Mechanical Diaphragm Calibration
This test calculates the gain calibration and offsets for each diaphragm. It does not use
radiation.
2 
Optical System Calibration
This test calculates the gain calibration and offsets for each leaf. It does not use radiation.
3 
Position of MV Detector Panel
4 
Pixel Size
This test calculates the ratio of millimeters at isocenter to MV detector panel pixels. The
workflow uses the ratio to display test results in millimeters at isocenter.
5 
Radiation Center
This test finds the center of rotation of the radiation beam.
6 
Diaphragm Calibration
This test does the fine calibration of the diaphragms. It finds the correct position of each
diaphragm from the radiation center.
7 
Leaf Calibration
This test does the fine calibration of the leaves. It finds the correct position of each leaf
from the radiation center.

Do the task to clean, and apply oil to, the jockey wheels on the gantry drum before you do this
task.
1 
Rotate the gantry to 180°.
2 
Make sure that the linear accelerator is in a balanced condition.
3 
Slowly rotate the gantry through 360° and at the same time make sure that only two of the

Do step 1 to 3 two times.

If all three of the jockey wheels touch the rim at a point in the rotation and a minimum of
one wheel cannot be freely rotated by hand, then follow the jockey wheel set up
procedure. Refer to the Corrective Maintenance Manual for the Movements System for
more information.

Examine the cable to make sure there are no signs of damage or deterioration.

Switch off the linear accelerator.
b
Use a calibrated crimp tool and a new crimp connector to make a new crimp.
c
Check that the cable cannot move in the crimp connector.
4 
If the cable is damaged:
a
Switch off the linear accelerator.
b
Replace the cable.
c
Apply a new crimp connector and check for tightness.

gearbox.

Look at the window in the gearbox to see the level of oil.
Note:
It is possible that the inner surface of the window has a mark to show the maximum level of oil.
This can give an incorrect indication of the level of oil.
a
If you can see oil in the window, then there is sufficient oil in the gearbox.
b
If you cannot see oil in the window, then add oil.
2 
Remove the breather plug.
3 
Add oil through the breather plug hole on the gearbox.
4 
Be careful not to add too much oil.
5 
Examine the surfaces below the gearbox and the bottom surface of the gearbox for signs of
oil. If there is a large leak:
a
You must find the cause of the leak.
b
Add more oil.
c
If necessary, see the Precise Treatment Table™ Corrective Maintenance Manual.

12.1
Introduction to the extended service life tasks
It is necessary to do regular planned maintenance and safety audit checks to keep the operation
of the system safe and satisfactory. The regular planned maintenance checks help to prevent a
sudden malfunction with subsequent repair and downtime of the equipment.
WARNING 12.1
Do not operate the equipment unless you correctly complete the safety checks, planned
maintenance schedules, and extended life checks. If you ignore this warning, you can cause
fatal injury and damage to the equipment.
This document gives the necessary procedures to do the planned maintenance checks for
extended service life, after 10 years of normal use.
The usual planned maintenance tasks continue after the 10 years of normal use. The additional
extended service life are then added to the planned maintenance schedule, in the frequency
specified for the extended service life checks.

WARNING 12.2
Do not work on the linear accelerator before you know the date and time of when the system
restart is scheduled. This is to make sure that the equipment will not become live, with high
voltages, while you are in the equipment. If you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury.
WARNING 12.3

linear accelerator can be configured to stay in an Initialized state when not in working hours. If
you ignore this warning, you can cause fatal injury.

13.1
Recording the planned maintenance results
An approved Elekta service engineer must record that the planned maintenance tasks were done,
and the applicable corrective actions, measurements, and results. The tool used to make the
measurement shall be recorded, this includes its serial number. The status of the result is usually
recorded as one of:
•
Not Applicable, A
•
Completed as specified
•
Done by customer, C
•
Test Fail, F, with the details why the check failed
•
Not done at customer request, N, with the name of the contact person who made the
request
•
Test Pass, P
•
Test Pass, P, following repair with the details of the repair
•
Not Done, X, with an explanation why the test was not done.
The Elekta Customer Lifecycle Management (CLM) system is usually the system that you use to

Note:

1 
Make a copy of the applicable Results list for the extended service life, and the applicable
monthly or annual PM check.

Use the procedures in this document to do checks that the system is operational after the
10 years or normal use. Make sure that a representative of the customer is available to
attend the checks.
The representative must sign and date the checklist when the tasks are completed.

When you complete a task, write in the Results list to show that the check has Passed or
Failed. If necessary, add corrective actions to the Comments column.
4 
When all the checks and tasks are completed, you and the User, or their representative,
must sign and date the Results list.
